# Decisions log

Decisions made autonomously while the owner was AFK. Each line: decision — reason.

## Owner-approved (2026-10-10)
- Locus theme: purple buttons use #280A38 text; dark-mode table header #533B60; code font JetBrains Mono; comment highlight keeps 2px stripe.
- Storage: `node:sqlite` + FTS5; migration is a script, tested on a copy of real data only.
- Cover images: PNG via @resvg/resvg-js. Real Slack unfurls are not tested.
- Single draft PR, one green commit per item. Security hardening out of scope.

## Defaults applied
- Named readers = self-declared reviewer name (no auth exists).
- Legacy sessions (no edit token) stay link-editable.
- GitHub Pages path routes via 404.html SPA fallback.

## Spec reconciliation (2026-10-10, see specs/00-cross-cutting.md and BUILD-ORDER.md)
- View toggle = one `view-toggle` group with `view-toggle-read|edit|split`, labels Read/Edit/Split — replaces Edit/Preview; existing `has-text("Edit")` selectors keep working, `"Preview"` ones move to `view-toggle-read`.
- `AppToast`/`AppMenu`/`useDocState`/`DocView` are built by #2 (first consumer), not #10/#1 — needed by the foundation wave.
- `EditorToolbar` owned by #8; `focus-mode-btn` lives in it (not the header) so it survives focus mode.
- Pasted table = 2 undo steps (raw paste, then pre-paste); slash insert = 1 step back to `/query`.
- One search endpoint: `GET /library/docs` (list + FTS, segment snippets); `GET /search` dropped; #20 implements it.
- `docTitle` precedence: sessionName > front-matter title / HTML `<title>` > first human-visible H1 > filename > Untitled (FE and server).
- Handed-out server URLs use `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` only when explicitly set, else `FRONTEND_URL`; FE-built links always use the page origin.
- Reader identity: `reader_id` (anon-uuid) for reactions/views; `reader_key` = `name:<lower name>` else reader_id for pins, header percent-encoded.
- Front-matter absolute line numbers fixed by #5 (first useMarkdown item), not #7.
- All UI view changes use `replaceState` (incl. slides entry); Back never steps through views.
- `?` shortcuts overlay only in edit/split views; Esc layering and z-index scale centralised in 00 §3.
- Viewers have no `share-btn`/share dialog; they use `copy-link-btn`.
- #20 (orchestrator): live data contains one corrupt stray file `oldformat12345.json` (a test artifact, not valid JSON). The migration keeps strict behaviour (reports it, exits non-zero); the PR's deploy steps tell the operator to delete that file first. The live data dir is never modified by the build.
- #2/#4 (orchestrator ruling): a pinned revision `/d/<id>@<hash>` never GETs the live `/paste/<id>` (AC-04.15 checks the pathname). It gets content from `/paste/<id>/revisions/<hash>`, comments from `/paste/<id>/comments`, approval from the approval endpoint, and the doc `mode` from a new additive `mode` field on the revision response (owned by #2).
- #2 (orchestrator ruling): menus focus the checked item if there is one, else the first (00 §3.2 wins over AC-02.17's wording).
- #2 (orchestrator ruling): #2 adds `data-testid="theme-toggle"` to the existing theme button; #1 then rebuilds the control around it.
- #2: durable-sync e2e expectations of a visible "✓ Saved" change to "save finished, save-state hidden" (spec rule 5); this is a listed pre-existing test change.

## Implementation decisions
- #4: UI view toggles do not write `?view=` yet — they *drop* a present `view` param (replaceState) so a reload/copied link cannot reopen a stale view; unknown/forbidden/empty values are rewritten to `view=read` and `?view=edit` is honoured on load. Writing the toggle into the URL reopens edit view after a reload, which breaks durable-sync.test.mjs:165-169 and :212-215 (they reload in edit view and expect `.preview-pane`) — #2/#7 (ViewToggle owners) wire it with that test change.
- #4: frame→parent `anchor-changed` with `id: ''` clears the fragment (rule 15's in-frame `href="#"`); otherwise only ids of 1–256 chars are accepted. Frame-driven fragment updates are coalesced to ≤ 2/s and dropped if the route changed meanwhile; every history call is try/caught (Safari throws past its rate limit).
- #4: one leave rule (rule 13): any navigation away from the attached shared doc with unsaved changes (link, Back/Forward, library, New, not-found) flushes autosave for ≤ 1.5 s while the doc stays on screen, then `confirm()`s. Cancel pushes the doc URL back; accepting discards the edits (detach + drop the persisted draft), so later navigation does not ask again.
- #4: drafts: the main draft slot only ever holds what the current route shows (paused otherwise), and the never-shared local draft also lives in its own slot (`md-review-local-draft`), so opening a shared doc never costs it. The landing route shows that local draft when arriving from elsewhere; sharing a local doc (or New on it) forgets it; New from a shared doc keeps it in storage. An all-empty screen writes nothing. Exception kept from before: a doc that answers 404/410 while this browser holds its draft turns that copy into the local doc.
- #4: slugs are matched case-sensitively by the server (`/d/Weekly` ≠ `/d/weekly` → doc-not-found); left as-is.
- #4: local-draft persistence is paused on pinned-revision, file and embed views so viewing them never overwrites the reader's own draft.
- #4: pinned and file routes use a read-only header (no Edit/Preview, Save, History, Share, Generate Prompt, New, rename); the pinned header shows the doc id as its name (the revision API has no filename).
- #4: a doc that answers 404/410 while this browser holds its draft keeps the "Showing your local copy" notice and moves to the landing route (replaceState), where a local doc lives.
- Build order (orchestrator): #20 lands before #2 instead of after it. #20 changes no frontend code and its golden tests treat `mode` as an allowed additive field. #2 was built against the JSON server and then ported onto #20's route modules: one helper, `server/mode.cjs` (validation, default, `modeOf` for legacy rows), used by paste-create, session (PUT meta + GETs), list, revisions and library-docs, on top of the pure `shared/docMode.mjs` that the FE uses too.
- #5 (test author): `src/composables/useDocTitle.ts` exports `docTitle({sessionName, content, contentType, filename})` (00 §5 order, whitespace collapsed, no truncation), `truncateTitle(title, max=80)` (cut + `…`), `formatDocumentTitle(title)` → `<title> · md-review`.
- #8 (test author): `src/composables/useExternalChange.ts` exports `minimalChange(oldText, newText)` → `null` when equal, else one `{from, to, insert}` covering only the changed span.
- #3 (test author): `src/markdown/headingIds.ts` exports `slugify(text)`, `assignIds(texts[])`, `extractHeadings(source)` → `{level,id,text}[]` (same ids as rendered), `buildToc(headings)` → `{id,text,level,depth}[]` (drops a lone leading H1, levels 1–3, `[]` when < 2). Slugs match github-slugger@2.0.0.
- #9 (test author): `src/editor/markdownCommands.ts` exports CodeMirror state commands `toggleBold`, `toggleItalic`, `toggleStrikethrough`, `toggleCode`, `toggleLink`.
- Scope add (orchestrator): QA on #4 found two PRE-EXISTING sync bugs (also on master 65d5a29). (1) Major: after a 412 conflict, a reload/close+reopen forgets the conflict state ("Unsaved changes"), and the next save PUTs with the collaborator's hash as If-Match and overwrites their change. (2) Minor: with saves failing, typing then reloading within ~300 ms loses the text (draft not flushed on pagehide). Both are assigned to #8, which owns useSync's remote-change handling; the conflict state must persist with the draft and survive reload.
- Scope add: at 390 px the doc header overflows and the view toggle is unreachable — covered by #2 (header) / #5 (phone header).

## Implementation decisions
- #20: a server that refuses to boot on an un-migrated data dir must not leave an (empty) DB file behind — otherwise the next boot would pass the check and silently 404 every link (AC-20.7 test asserts it).
- #20: golden compatibility (AC-20.3) is checked against responses frozen from the JSON-file server at 592efa6 (`server/test-items/fixtures/20/goldens.json`); allowed differences are ETag values, run-generated ids/timestamps, file-list order (legacy order is readdir order), 400 instead of the legacy 500 for an invalid `/paste/list?name=` regex, `content_hash`/`comments: []` added where legacy omitted them, the additive keys of rule 5 / 00 §10.5, and `mode` per 00 §1.4 — because these are the only differences the spec allows or that are filesystem noise.
- #20: a slug present in both `_slug-index.json` (session) and `_site-index.json` (site) keeps the legacy split: `slugs` row points at the session, the site still resolves by its own `sites.slug` — matches the JSON server's `resolveId` / `resolveSiteId`.
- #20: a site directory with no `_site-index.json` entry (the live data has one) is still served at `/site/<id>/` and stays out of `/site/list`, as the JSON server does.
- #20: a corrupt revision blob in the DB answers 500 `…unreadable…`, never empty content — the DB-era form of `server/test.mjs:550-562`.
- #20: `match.field` names where the snippet came from. A title (else filename) hit is shown unless the body excerpt has hit words the title does not show, case aside ("café" for a "Cafe notes" title — R-20.6 expects that body hit); then the body excerpt is shown with `field: content`. Snippets are plain text (markdown syntax stripped, whitespace collapsed, HTML entities decoded) and the body scan is capped at 256 KB per result.
- #20: snippets are cut in JS with a unicode61-like folding tokenizer instead of FTS5 `snippet()`/`highlight()` — those are quadratic in the number of hits (a 5 MB doc with 220k hits took 142 s; now 14 ms).
- #20: `/library/docs` answers 400 `{error:'invalid mode'|'invalid type'|'invalid updated_after'}` for malformed values (00 §8 only names sort/cursor); unknown collection/tag → `items: []` as specified. The cursor is an opaque offset bound to q + filters + effective sort; a different `limit` with a cursor is allowed.
- #20: library `updated_at` (sort + `updated_after`) is what `/paste/list` always reported: latest revision `at_end || at`, else `sharedAt`; comment/approval/meta writes do not bump it.
- #20: `POST /paste` stores `mode` (00 §1.4 default; an invalid value fell back to the default; since #2 it is a 400) and the creator's `author` as `created_by`; `GET /paste/:id` returns `mode` (additive) but not `created_by` (#26 exposes it).
- #20: legacy sessions that never stored a `content_hash` keep omitting it and are not seeded from '' on their first write (`contents.hashless`) — what the JSON server did.
- #20: every slug delete is scoped to its owner (`AND target_id = ?`): deleting a site or session, or releasing a slug via `PUT /meta`, never frees another doc's slug (the JSON server dropped index entries by name).
- #20: the migration skips a session whose revision blob is missing, unreadable or does not match its hash (reported under `errors`, exit ≠ 0) rather than importing it without that revision.
- #20: `GET /paste/list?name=<invalid regex>` → 400 `{error:'Invalid name pattern'}` (legacy 500); `GET /paste/:id` ETag = md5(id, write version, content hash), so it changes on every write including file writes.
- #20: client-supplied meta keys named like server-managed columns (`edit_token_hash`, `upsert_key`, `created_by`, `from_template_json`, `version`, `title`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `id`, …) are dropped on write and by the migration, never kept in `extra_json` — a forged `edit_token_hash` must not round-trip.
- #20: the migration is a pre-cutover tool: each session is written and verified in one transaction (rolled back on failure); `schema_meta.migration_complete` is set only after a run whose only errors are reported corrupt sources, and the server refuses to boot on a DB whose migration started but did not complete (even with `ALLOW_EMPTY_DB=1`). A session the server wrote after migration (`version > 1`) is reported `diverged` and left alone; a session deleted after cutover would be re-imported by a re-run, so the script is not run after cutover.
- #20 (perf): the indexed text, snippet text and docTitle are computed in linear time — tags, comments, raw-text elements and markdown links are found with forward-only indexOf scans, `_emphasis_` and ATX headings are parsed by hand, and the table-delimiter and list-bullet rules no longer rescan across lines (the regex versions took 6–122 s on 600 KB docs such as `'<script'×90k` or `'[a'×300k`). Output is unchanged on the #20 fixtures, the repo docs, the live data dir and 100k fuzzed inputs compared against the regex versions.
- #22: the bundled fonts are static Regular/SemiBold instances cut (fontTools instancer) from google/fonts `ofl/montserrat/Montserrat[wght].ttf` — google/fonts ships only the variable file and resvg ignores variable axes (every weight rendered as Thin); OFL.txt is bundled beside them. System fonts are never loaded.
- #22: the cover draws only what the bundled font can: emoji (incl. ZWJ sequences, modifiers, flags, variation selectors, keycaps) and characters Montserrat has no glyph for are removed from the cover title and author; when no letter or digit is left the cover shows the filename (without extension), else "Markdown document"/"HTML document". cover_key is computed from the drawn title and meta line, so two docs whose covers look the same share a key. Page text (og:title etc.) is unaffected.
- #22: the meta page ETag also covers `article:modified_time`, the redirect target (query) and the canonical URL, not only (title, description, cover_key, variant) — otherwise a body edit or another query string could answer 304 with a stale page. `If-None-Match: *` answers 304 for an existing doc (page and cover).
- #22: the cover's "Updated" date is the UTC day of `updated_at`; "by" is the first non-seeded revision's author, else `created_by` — never a client label (api/mcp/ui); it is left out when unknown and cut with "…" when it would push the date off the cover.
- #22: `/d/:x/:file` pages describe the file itself (its own docTitle/description for .md/.markdown/.txt/.html files; a "file from …" line otherwise) and reuse the doc's cover. Pinned `/d/:x@:rev` pages describe that revision (its title, description and revision time) and carry no og:image (`twitter:card summary`) — the only cover is the live doc's, which could contradict the revision. An unknown revision or unlisted file is the doc's 404 page; an unparseable `/d/` path (dot or empty segments, encoded slashes, `@rev` plus a file, a malformed rev) is a 404 page that sends humans to the app root `FRONTEND_URL/d/`, never echoing the raw path.
- #22: meta-page and cover text look at the first 256 KB of a doc (`SCAN_CAP`); HTML is scanned with indexOf (no lazy cross-tag regexes), line/paragraph regexes see at most 1 KB, and rule 4c looks for the first visible paragraph among the first 500 blocks — so extraction is linear (a 1 MB pathological doc < 50 ms). The H1 title now decodes entities and honours backslash escapes (also in the #20 search title); a leading BOM is ignored; a doc without `contentType` named `*.html`/`*.htm` is treated as HTML for the meta page and cover.
- #22: one link rule: `POST /paste` and `GET /paste/:id` (full, or `?fields=` with meta) return `url` = `handedOutUrl(slug || id)` (`server/links.cjs`); MCP `shareUrl` and CLI `url` use the backend's `url` and fall back to `docUrl(PUBLIC_BASE_URL || FRONTEND_URL, x)` from their own env for an older backend. An explicit CLI `--frontend` wins over both. The HTTP MCP server reads PUBLIC_BASE_URL too.
- #2: save-state renders in the editor header only (00 §2.2 wins over #2 rule 5's "all columns" row); the read view shows conflicts through `conflict-bar` as before. durable-sync's restore test now watches the server instead of a read-view save-state.
- #2: on a pinned revision of a review doc (viewer) the sidebar lists the doc's comments (`GET /paste/:id/comments`) and the approval banner shows the doc's status with "Open the latest version to approve or request changes" instead of actions (an approval from an old revision was misleading, and local-only resolves could enable a button the server then refused). Selecting text does not start a new comment — its line numbers would anchor to an old revision — and sidebar edits stay local (no live session before #23).
- #2: History on a pinned revision compares against that revision ("now" = what is on screen); the default "from" is the revision before it. Restore stays editor-only.
- #2: file routes (`/d/:x/:file`) keep #4's viewer capability and open in publish mode (a session file has no comments of its own); revisit with #26/#23.
- #2: the History revision count and unseen-changes dot moved onto the `menu-history` item (badge + `.history-dot`); `history-button` is retired.
- #2: `AppMode` is now `'upload' | 'doc' | 'dashboard'`; usePersistence's callback keeps its old `'review'` value (mapped to `'doc'` in useDocState) so its unit tests stay untouched.
- #2: a mode PUT in flight, or one that settled after a poll's request started, wins over that poll's `mode` (no flicker back on a fast toggle); the server value is authoritative from the next poll on.
- #2: phone (<641px) demotes app-home-link, nav-library, reviewer-name, share-btn and copy-link-btn to the overflow menu and makes the view toggle icon-only; tablet demotes reviewer-name; reader meta moves to `doc-meta-row` below 1100px. #5 owns the rest of the phone layout.
- #2: the pinned-revision header title is the doc's sessionName || filename: `GET /paste/:id/revisions/:hash` additively returns `sessionName` and `filename` next to `mode` (same reason as the mode ruling: a pinned revision never GETs /paste/<id>).
- #2: the below-header stack renders in 00 §2.4 order (pinned → conflict/persist-error → notice → approval/summary → changes); before #2 approval/summary/changes came above the notice and conflict bars.
- #2: mode writes are serialised (one PUT in flight; the latest choice is written next; a failure rolls back with a toast only if nothing newer is pending, so no error toast when the final state succeeded).
- #2: FE + server share `shared/docMode.mjs` (00 §4.8) through a new `@shared` alias (vite + tsconfig paths; a `.d.mts` gives the FE its types); the server loads it with `require()` (Node ≥ 22 `require(esm)`).
- #2: toasts keep their status/alert role but set `aria-live="off"`; two always-present sr-only live regions (polite, assertive) announce the newest toast text, and hovering or focusing a toast pauses its auto-dismiss.
- #2: the leave-page handlers (beforeunload/pagehide/visibilitychange autosave flush) moved from App.vue into useAutosave; the comment-file import errors use toasts instead of alert().
- #6: the editor slot is a thin `LazyEditor.vue` wrapper (placeholder / error / retry, attrs passed through to EditorPane) over one shared loader (`useEditorLoader.ts`), not a bare `defineAsyncComponent` — retry and the stale-deploy diagnosis need state `defineAsyncComponent` doesn't expose, and EditorPane stays untouched apart from an exposed `focus()`.
- #6: retry re-imports the EditorPane URL named in the failed import's error with a `?retry=N` cache-bust (browsers keep failed module fetches) and takes the component from `default` (or the export whose `__name` is EditorPane); after a failure, hover/focus prefetch stays quiet until an explicit Edit/Retry. "Stale deployment" = a `HEAD` on that URL returns 404/410; when the error names no URL (Safari), a no-store fetch of index.html whose entry script differs from the running one. A network error = offline, no reload hint. Focus moves into the editor only on its first mount, not on later warm read → edit switches (same as before #6, where a fresh editor never took focus).
- #6: `vite.config.ts` puts every node_modules module EditorPane statically needs (and the entry doesn't) into a `codemirror` vendor chunk (`manualChunks`, computed from the module graph; Vite's preload helper pinned to its own tiny chunk so the entry never imports the vendor chunk). The EditorPane chunk is then a 4 kB facade with a `default` export and the language-data chunks import CodeMirror from the vendor chunk, so a cache-busted retry never creates a second CodeMirror.
- #6: the kept-alive editor is keyed on the doc on screen (`screenKey|pasteId`): another document drops the instance (and any per-doc editor state such as #8 history); a local doc replaced through the file picker keeps the `landing` key and therefore the instance (its v-model content is replaced).
- #23: a `?edit=` token is held in memory until the doc's GET (sent with it) answers `access.can_edit: true`, and only then stored, under the `id` the GET returned — a token for another doc is never stored; a stored token a GET no longer accepts is dropped — rule 9 + the "token for a different doc" edge case.
- #23: GET /paste/:id's ETag varies with the caller's access on protected docs (view vs edit), and rotation/claim bumps the session version — otherwise a poller's 304 would keep a stale `access` after a rotation.
- #23: chunk/complete only accept an upload started on the same doc (else 404 "Upload not found"), and uploadIds must be hex — otherwise chunks could be pushed into a protected doc's upload through a legacy doc's URL, bypassing the guard.
- #23: the expiry picker preselects the value last applied in this dialog, else "Never" for a doc without expiry, else the smallest option covering the time left — the server stores only `expires_at`, not the chosen day count; the label always shows the real date.
- #23: opening History on a live doc refreshes the revision list, and Escape closes the History and Share dialogs — AC-23.9 waits for the list request and closes History with Escape.
- #23: pre-#23 test suites keep their intent through one mechanism each: e2e suites create link-editable (legacy) docs via `tests/e2e/lib/legacy-docs.mjs`; server suites opt in to `server/test-items/lib/edit-token-jar.mjs`, which presents each doc's own token on writes. #23's own tests use neither.
- #23: verify.sh exports `MCP_TOKEN_STORE` under the run dir so no test writes the repo default `server/mcp-state/`.
- #23 (review round): losing edit access — a write refused with 401/403 or a poll answering `can_edit: false` — runs one handler: view-only toast (once), viewer, read view, `?view=edit|split` rewritten to `view=read`.
- #23 (review round): edits that never reached the server when a doc turns view-only become an unsaved *local copy* (`md-review-local-copies` localStorage map, {[docId]: {markdown, filename, at}}), shown in a banner below the header ("Your unsaved changes (not on the server)", testids `local-copy-banner|toggle|copy|download|discard|body`) while the doc shows the server version; a reload as viewer turns an unsaved draft into that copy too. The copy renders inside `.preview-pane` (the shared preview styles), expanded by default.
- #23 (review round): for a viewer, autosave, keepalive writes on pagehide, the leave-page prompt and the discard confirmation are skipped; a 401/403 save is not a save error.
- #23 (review round): useEditToken's router hook is registered explicitly by App.vue (`installEditTokenHook()` before `router.bootstrap()`), not as an import side effect.
- #23 (review round): e2e `createDoc({ protected: true })` returns `editToken` (open with `?edit=`); the legacy default stays for unrelated suites. The #6 lazy-chunk part of the viewer ACs waits for #6; 23-fixes checks that a protected viewer never gets an editor.
- #23: MCP token-store keys are `${pasteApiUrl}|${idOrSlug}` (trailing slash trimmed); bare pre-scoping keys are read as a fallback and replaced by the scoped key on the next save of that doc — two backends' docs with the same id or slug must not share a token.
- #23: token-store writes take an O_EXCL lock file (`${file}.lock`; stale after 5 s; after 3 s of waiting the writer goes ahead) and re-read + merge before the atomic rename — concurrent stdio/HTTP MCP processes must not drop each other's entries.
- #23: MCP shell commands use `PASTE_PUBLIC_URL`, else `PASTE_API_URL` (both transports); the hard-coded `10.0.99.151:3100` default is removed; trailing slashes in the configured URLs are ignored.
- #23: GET /paste/:id sends `Vary: Authorization, X-Edit-Token` (200 and 304); create and rotate/claim responses are `Cache-Control: no-store` (they carry the raw token). The #20 golden comparison accepts that header on token-carrying responses.
- #23 (integration): a viewer never keeps #6's hidden editor — `editorShown` requires capability editor and losing edit access unmounts the kept editor slot.
- #8: write origin is explicit — writers call `markExternalChange(text, 'remote'|'local')` (useExternalChange.ts) right before assigning `markdown`; an unmarked external write is treated as remote (minimal change, out of history, history cleared). Only revision restore is marked `local` (one line in DocView.vue's restore handler).
- #8: until #6/#7 keep the editor mounted, history survives a Read↔Edit switch by keeping the editor's selection + history (`state.toJSON({history})`) on unmount and restoring it on the next mount, only for the same text and when no barrier (remote write, pasteId change) happened meanwhile. Works unchanged if #6 keeps the instance alive.
- #8: the SVG paste handler moved from EditorPane into `src/editor/svgPaste.ts` (listed in extensions.ts) so later paste modules slot in by order; it is tagged `input.paste`, and every paste/drop is history-isolated by a transactionExtender.
- #8 (scope add 1): a conflicted draft persists `serverMarkdown` = the copy the edits were based on, its `baseHash`, and `conflict: true`; on load `restoreDraft` keeps that base as the If-Match baseline and the fresh server copy as the remote side (before, the fresh copy became the baseline, so the next reload showed "Unsaved changes" and the next save overwrote the collaborator).
- #8 (scope add 2): on pagehide / beforeunload / visibilitychange→hidden the draft snapshot is also written synchronously to localStorage (existing keys `md-review-state` / `md-review-local-draft`); the next load takes whichever of that and the IndexedDB copy has the newer `savedAt`, then removes the localStorage copy. Snapshots too big for localStorage still get the async IndexedDB attempt.
- #8 (fix round): document undo/redo runs only while the editor has focus or from the toolbar. Chrome forwards a native undo/redo pressed in another text field (filename, reviewer name) with nothing left to undo there to the last edited contenteditable as a `historyUndo`/`historyRedo` beforeinput; a highest-precedence handler swallows those when the editor is not focused. App's only global key handler is Mod+S.
- #8 (fix round): remote writes are applied as one change per changed region (`minimalChanges`: line diff of the span between common prefix/suffix via `diff`, each hunk trimmed to its differing characters, all in one transaction), so a caret or scroll anchor between distant edits maps through untouched. More than 2000 changed lines falls back to the single span. `minimalChange` (single span, frozen contract) is unchanged.
- #8 (fix round): a revision restore done from Read view is not undoable until #6 keeps the editor mounted — the restored text differs from the kept editor state, so the next Edit view starts with a fresh history.
- #8 (fix round): multi-cursor is not enabled (CodeMirror's `allowMultipleSelections` stays off), so the "multi-cursor edit undone in one step" edge case does not apply; enabling it is a separate product call.
- #8 (fix round): every local document switch (file load, New/reset, landing local draft) calls `historyBarrier()`, so history kept across a view switch never comes back for a different doc with identical text. The localStorage flush copy is removed once the async write of that same snapshot lands; the beforeunload flush listener was dropped (pagehide covers reload, close and bfcache). Since #2 there is one leave-page path: useAutosave's pagehide / visibilitychange→hidden handler first calls `usePersistence.flushDraft()` (synchronous local-draft copy), then sends dirty shared edits with keepalive; usePersistence registers no window listeners of its own.
- #9: Tab/Shift+Tab renumber the ordered lists they touch in the same undo step: a nested ordered list counts from 1 (CommonMark lets only `1.` interrupt the parent item's paragraph, so `   2. b` under `1. a` would render as text), a top-level one keeps its first number and stays consecutive; siblings left behind by an outdent restart at 1 under the moved item. Nested lists that started at another number are reset to 1 when touched.
- #9: multi-cursor stays off in the editor (#8 decision); the commands act on every range (unit-tested with `allowMultipleSelections`), so turning it on later needs no change here.
- #9: the overlay's focus trap is inline in `ShortcutsOverlay.vue` until #3's `useFocusTrap` exists. `?` opens it only while an `EditorToolbar` is on screen (registered host element with client rects) — the editor may stay mounted but hidden (#6 keep-alive), so mounted is not enough; the `?` entry (`shortcutsHelpShortcut`) is one line in App.vue's `useGlobalShortcuts` list and does its own gating/preventDefault so a `?` typed into an input is never swallowed.
- #9: the shortcuts button's overlay returns focus to the button on close (AC-09.16), the one exception to "toolbar buttons refocus the editor" (00 §3.3).
- #9 (fix round): block markup (`> `, `#…# `, `- `/`* `/`+ `, `N.`/`N)`, task box) stays outside emphasis/link/code markers, single- and multi-line. A selection that already contains the marker (`**a** and **b**`) is made one span — inner markers removed, whole wrapped — like Docs bolding a partly bold selection; a multi-line toggle decides wrap/unwrap once, from the first non-empty line. Mod+E unfences only when both fences belong to one FencedCode node. Mod+K escapes `[`/`]` in the label (and unescapes on unwrap).
- #9 (fix round): EditorPane's deferred selection report clamps its position to the current doc and skips a destroyed view (pre-existing "No tile at position N" page error when the doc shrank before the next frame); toolbar Undo/Redo titles now come from shortcutList's `formatCombo`, same labels and order as the overlay.
- #8 (landing on #6): `historyBarrier()` also clears a mounted editor's live history (`onHistoryBarrier` → `clearHistory`), because #6 keeps one editor instance across a local file replacement on the landing key and identical text never reaches the content watcher. #8's keep/restore-across-unmount stays (still used when #6's keyed instance is dropped and re-created for the same doc, gated by text + epoch); it is redundant for plain Read↔Edit switches now and could be removed later. (Code amended into the #8 commit; this line is uncommitted with #9.)
